hive.title: HIVE · system architecture
hive.scope: HIVE turns a robot's own code into a reviewed capability profile, represents each robot as an embodied agent, and lets one Executive coordinate the team through a shared world model. Safety-critical control stays on each robot.

nodes.label: Robot source code
nodes.detail: The robot's ROS 2 workspace and interface documentation are the onboarding input.

nodes.label: Composer + capability profile
nodes.detail: Collects line-level interface evidence and drafts a structured capability profile — skills, topics, limits — for human review.

nodes.label: Embodied agents
nodes.detail: Each onboarded robot is represented by an agent that exposes only its reviewed capabilities.

nodes.label: Shared world model
nodes.detail: Every robot reports observations and state into one shared task context.

nodes.label: Executive
nodes.detail: Breaks a plain-language mission into tasks, assigns them to capable robots, and validates each step against the world model before dispatch.

nodes.label: Robot-local controls
nodes.detail: Navigation, flight, manipulation, and emergency stop stay on the robot.

robotic-arm.title: Voice or text command → simulated pick-and-place
robotic-arm.scope: Speak or type a plain-English instruction. The agent turns it into manipulation skills and differential-IK motion on a simulated 7-DOF Franka Panda in MuJoCo.

nodes.label: Voice or typed command
nodes.detail: Hold the mic button and speak, or type — “put the red box on the shelf.” faster-whisper transcribes speech locally on the CPU.

nodes.label: Language agent
nodes.detail: A local parser handles common phrasing; NVIDIA NIM tool calling resolves ambiguous requests.

nodes.label: Manipulation skills
nodes.detail: Sequences look, find, pick, and place for the requested object and destination.

nodes.label: Differential IK
nodes.detail: mink differential IK, with a damped-least-squares fallback, drives the arm toward each target pose.

nodes.label: MuJoCo scene
nodes.detail: Franka Panda, gripper, table, shelf, and four colored boxes. Object poses come from simulator state; grasps use a weld constraint.

nodes.label: Scene + wrist cameras
nodes.detail: Rendered views answer look-at-the-scene questions through NIM vision.

ros2-micromouse-sync.title: Known maze · two synchronized simulators
ros2-micromouse-sync.scope: One flood-fill solution drives two simulators at once: the mms micromouse interface and a Gazebo Harmonic robot, kept in step through ROS 2.

nodes.label: Generated maze specification
nodes.detail: A seeded 16 × 16 maze, goal, and cell geometry feed the solver and both simulators.

nodes.label: Flood-fill planner
nodes.detail: Computes the distance field over the full maze and walks the gradient to the goal.

nodes.label: mms interface
nodes.detail: Displays flood-fill distances and executes moves through the mms text protocol.

nodes.label: ROS 2 cell-motion controller
nodes.detail: Drains queued moves one cell at a time and publishes the current cell.

nodes.label: Gazebo Harmonic
nodes.detail: Moves the robot cell by cell with exact pose updates, mirroring the planner.

nodes.label: Live path / cell view
nodes.detail: Shows the planned path and the robot's current cell beside the maze.

autonomous-drone.title: Quadcopter · flight-controller interfaces
autonomous-drone.scope: Signal interfaces between the SpeedyBee F7 Mini flight controller and its peripherals. A passive carrier board breaks out the low-voltage lines; video and motor power run on their own paths.

nodes.label: Flight controller
nodes.detail: SpeedyBee F7 Mini running Betaflight.

nodes.label: Peripheral carrier board
nodes.detail: Passive low-voltage breakout that routes flight-controller UART and PWM lines to peripheral connectors.

nodes.label: GPS · ELRS · gimbal servo
nodes.detail: GPS on UART2, ELRS receiver on UART3, and the single-axis gimbal servo on PWM5.

nodes.label: Camera module
nodes.detail: Compact FPV camera on the tilt gimbal; analog video goes straight to the VTX.

nodes.label: Video transmitter
nodes.detail: RushFPV Tiny Tank, with camera video in and a UART4 control link.

nodes.label: 4-in-1 ESC
nodes.detail: Motor power stays off the carrier board; only the flight controller's ESC signal is shown.

amphibious-robot.title: Amphibious robot · mechanical layout
amphibious-robot.scope: Four ring frames carry the propellers around a central electronics bay. The laser-cut structure ties them together and sets the load paths for flying, driving, and swimming.

nodes.label: Laser-cut frame
nodes.detail: Sheet-cut arms and decks join the four rings to the central bay and carry thrust, ground, and water loads.

nodes.label: Central electronics bay
nodes.detail: Compute and power electronics packaged at the center of mass.

nodes.label: Ring + propeller assemblies
nodes.detail: Each ring frame encloses a motor and propeller mounted on the frame arms.

nodes.label: Fly · drive · swim
nodes.detail: One airframe designed to operate in air, on the ground, and in water.

nodes.label: Frame material trade study
nodes.detail: Compares six frame sheet materials on stiffness and strength per weight, water durability, impact toughness, and in-house manufacturability.

jarvis-agentic-orchestrator.title: Jarvis · request to answer
jarvis-agentic-orchestrator.scope: A thin FastAPI sidecar wires chat, voice, and tools to the OpenJarvis engine. Every model call goes through one LiteLLM path with a fallback ladder; hard planning escalates to a three-model council.

nodes.label: Chat + voice
nodes.detail: Typed chat, or the always-on “Hey Jarvis” wake word with faster-whisper speech-to-text and Edge-TTS replies.

nodes.label: FastAPI sidecar
nodes.detail: Connects every feature to the OpenJarvis backbone without modifying it.

nodes.label: Router + fallback ladder
nodes.detail: Classifies each task, then walks NIM → NIM → Gemini Flash → local Ollama with exponential backoff.

nodes.label: Planning council + agent graph
nodes.detail: Three model families propose in parallel and a reasoning model synthesizes one plan; user-drawn agent graphs run in topological order, at most three at a time.

nodes.label: MCP tools
nodes.detail: Live code knowledge graph, web and GitHub access, and six action tools.

nodes.label: Memory
nodes.detail: Durable personal facts and session history, carried across model switches.

act-training.title: ACT training · LeRobot toolchain
act-training.scope: A reproducible LeRobot pipeline on public SO-101 data: lock the environment, train ACT for 10,000 steps, reload the checkpoint in a fresh process, and run GPU inference.

nodes.label: Public SO-101 dataset
nodes.detail: lerobot/svla_so101_pickplace supplies recorded observations and actions.

nodes.label: Locked LeRobot environment
nodes.detail: LeRobot 0.5.0, PyTorch, and CUDA 12.8 on WSL2, checked before training.

nodes.label: ACT training run
nodes.detail: 10,000-step Action Chunking Transformer run, completed with exit code 0.

nodes.label: Saved checkpoint
nodes.detail: Training output written locally for the reload check.

nodes.label: Fresh-process reload + inference
nodes.detail: A separate script reloads the checkpoint and runs GPU inference.

nodes.label: Task-success evaluation
nodes.detail: The next stage — success rates on SO-101 tasks. Paused in September 2026.
